newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open higher as results, GDP please.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open higher as results, GDP please.

text.p: French shares opened higher, despite an overnight fall on Wall Street on hawkish remarks by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan, as the fourth quarter French GDP and corporate results pleased, dealers said.
Brokers said the increased probability of an interest rate rise in the U.S. could prompt investment funds to switch some money to Europe and lead them to buy French paper.
A rise in the dollar was also supporting shares.
On technical terms, analysts said the underlying upward trend had not been broken by Wednesday's 0.21 percent fall.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 15.79 points or 0.61 percent at 2,617.96 at 0907 GMT
"After Greenspan's statements and the drop on Wall Street, we were bracing for a decline today. But the GDP is a positive surprise," another broker said.
The February CAC-40 future was trading 14 points higher at 2,617 on GLOBEX at 0828 GMT.
French GDP rose 0.2 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996 after a revised 0.8 percent rise in the third quarter, giving full-year growth of 1.3 percent, INSEE said.
"There are clear signs of export-led growth, a classic style of recovery, and the early signs of recovery in the first quarter are fairly evident," an analyst said.

L'Oreal was up 0.81 percent at 1,990 after its 1996 net profit before capital gains/losses and after minority interests rose to 3.73 billion francs from 3.38 billion francs. "This increase was achieved despite the rise in interest expenses due to acquisitions," L'Oreal said.
Paribas, up 1.77 percent at 402 francs, turned in a 1996 net attributable profit of 4.35 billion francs against a loss of four billion.
Gan was suspended at 123 francs pending a statement. UIC also suspened for the day.
